history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - Christian (Anglican) church; keep-or-drop decision needed. Designed by Colonel J. T. Boileau in 1844; the cornerstone was laid on 9 September 1844 by Bishop Daniel Wilson, Bishop of Calcutta, and the church was consecrated on 10 January 1857 to serve the Anglican British community of Simla. Built in neo-Gothic style on The Ridge at a cost of Rs 40,000-50,000. The clock was donated by Colonel Dumbleton in 1860; the porch was added in 1873; a British-made pipe organ was installed in 1899 and renovated in 1932. The chancel stained-glass window was designed by Lockwood Kipling. Conflict: one travel source names Bishop Wilson of Calcutta as the consecrator, against Wikipedia's Bishop Thomas Daltrey, Bishop of Madras. Reputedly the second-oldest church in North India after St. John's Church, Meerut. Featured in Bollywood films such as Black and 3 Idiots. Worship is conducted in Hindi and English; the present head priest is Rev. Sohan Lal.

name: Christ Church, Shimla
town_description: Shimla is the capital of Himachal Pradesh and a hill station in the north-western Himalayas. It was the summer capital of British India and remains one of India's best-known hill resorts, centred on The Ridge and The Mall.
tradition: Anglican Christianity (built for the Anglican British community; services in Hindi and English)

travel.railway: Shimla railway station on the Kalka-Shimla narrow-gauge line (~2 km)
travel.road: On The Ridge in the heart of Shimla, off The Mall Road

visitor_information.best_time: March-June; December-February for snowfall; September-November for clear views
